explanation: An ellipse is the set of points whose distances to two fixed foci add to a constant. a and b are the semi-axes (half-widths) along x and y; when a = b you get a circle. The foci sit on the longer axis at distance c = √|a² − b²| from the center — the more a and b differ, the more stretched (eccentric) the ellipse.
bullets: a and b are the semi-axis lengths along x and y; a = b is a circle.
Foci lie on the major axis at c = √|a² − b²| from the center.
Sum of distances to the two foci is constant for every point.
